diff --git a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/duty_legs.py b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/duty_legs.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..ecb3c6b38f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/duty_legs.py
@@ -0,0 +1,236 @@
+"""The legs a plan step is served in, the switches between them, and what a stop costs.
+
+One concern with one owner, on ``plan_step.py``'s own argument: the pump
+arbiter serves a planned both step as a hot-water leg and a heating leg, and
+the optimizer prices the switches that serving makes, so two modules need one
+rule and neither may import the other. A leaf: numpy, the plan's running rule
+and the step width, nothing of Home Assistant.
+
+A switch between duties at constant draw is invisible to the cycling term,
+which prices the swing of the combined draw. On an install whose compressor
+stops at such a switch (pull request 3420, Bankaifan: hot water to heating,
+three times out of three) the stop turns the swing ``|a - b|`` into ``a + b``.
+The difference, ``2 * min(a, b)``, is ``min(a, b) / p_max`` cycles in the
+cycling term's own unit, and that is the weight a switch carries here, taken
+with the learned probability that the direction stops the compressor.
+
+A pair of per-direction values is always ``(hot water to heating, heating to
+hot water)``.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from .batchmath import row_sums
+from .plan_step import PLAN_STEP_MINUTES
+from .thermal_model import MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW
+
+#: The shortest single-duty share of a both step; a shorter share goes to
+#: the other duty for the whole step (valve travel and compressor cycling).
+SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES = 5.0
+
+#: Leg codes of :func:`leg_ends`.
+IDLE, SPACE, DHW = 0, 1, 2
+
+
+def both_step_legs(
+    space_kw: float, dhw_kw: float, step_minutes: float = PLAN_STEP_MINUTES
+) -> tuple[tuple[str, float], ...]:
+    """The legs of a step both circuits run in, in order, each with its minutes.
+
+    Hot water's share is the step's hot-water power over its total (tvofi,
+    2026-09-27); a share under :data:`SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES` on either side
+    collapses the step onto the other duty. Hot water goes first.
+    """
+    dhw_min = step_minutes * dhw_kw / (space_kw + dhw_kw)
+    if dhw_min < SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES:
+        return (("space", step_minutes),)
+    if step_minutes - dhw_min < SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES:
+        return (("dhw", step_minutes),)
+    return (("dhw", dhw_min), ("space", step_minutes - dhw_min))
+
+
+def _runs(kw: np.ndarray, floor: float | None) -> np.ndarray:
+    """``planned_draw_runs`` for one circuit, elementwise (pinned equal by test)."""
+    on = kw > MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW
+    return on if floor is None else on & ~(kw < floor)
+
+
+def leg_ends(
+    space_kw: Any,
+    dhw_kw: Any,
+    floor: float | None = None,
+    step_minutes: float = PLAN_STEP_MINUTES,
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
+    """Per step: the first leg, the last leg, and whether the step has two.
+
+    The arbiter's rule elementwise: ``step_duty`` reads each circuit alone
+    against the plan's ``floor``, and a both step splits by
+    :func:`both_step_legs`. ``space_kw`` may be a ``[B, n]`` batch against one
+    ``[n]`` hot-water plan.
+    """
+    space = np.asarray(space_kw, dtype=float)
+    dhw = np.asarray(dhw_kw, dtype=float)
+    s_on, d_on = _runs(space, floor), _runs(dhw, floor)
+    both = s_on & d_on
+    dhw_min = step_minutes * dhw / np.where(both, space + dhw, 1.0)
+    to_space = both & (dhw_min < SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES)
+    to_dhw = both & ~to_space & (step_minutes - dhw_min < SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES)
+    two = both & ~to_space & ~to_dhw
+    single = np.where(
+        (s_on & ~d_on) | to_space, SPACE, np.where((d_on & ~s_on) | to_dhw, DHW, IDLE)
+    )
+    return np.where(two, DHW, single), np.where(two, SPACE, single), two
+
+
+def priced_pair(values: Any, upper: float = math.inf) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """A per-direction pair as two floats in ``[0, upper]``, else zero."""
+    try:
+        pair = [float(v) for v in values]
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return 0.0, 0.0
+    if len(pair) != 2:
+        return 0.0, 0.0
+    a, b = (max(v, 0.0) if math.isfinite(v) and v <= upper else 0.0 for v in pair)
+    return a, b
+
+
+#: A boundary pairs each step but the last with the step after it; the legs
+#: that meet there and the levels they run at are read through the same pair.
+_BEFORE, _AFTER = np.s_[:, :-1], np.s_[:, 1:]
+
+
+def switch_weights_batch(
+    space_matrix: np.ndarray,
+    dhw_kw: np.ndarray,
+    stop_probability: tuple[float, float],
+    p_max: float,
+    floor: float | None = None,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Expected compressor stops at duty switches, in cycles, per row of plans.
+
+    Every pair of consecutive legs of different duty with no idle step
+    between weighs ``p * level / p_max``: inside a two-leg step both legs run
+    at the step's combined level; across a boundary the stop adds the smaller
+    of the two levels. ``row_sums`` reduces each row on its own, so a row is
+    :func:`switch_weight` of that plan bit for bit.
+    """
+    space = np.asarray(space_matrix, dtype=float)
+    p_ds, p_sd = stop_probability
+    if p_max <= 0:
+        return np.zeros(space.shape[0])
+    first, last, two = leg_ends(space, dhw_kw, floor)
+    level = space + np.asarray(dhw_kw, dtype=float)
+    before, after = last[_BEFORE], first[_AFTER]
+    stops = np.where(
+        (before == DHW) & (after == SPACE),
+        p_ds,
+        np.where((before == SPACE) & (after == DHW), p_sd, 0.0),
+    )
+    across = stops * np.minimum(level[_BEFORE], level[_AFTER])
+    inside = np.where(two, p_ds * level, 0.0)
+    return row_sums(np.concatenate([inside, across], axis=1)) / p_max
+
+
+def switch_weight(
+    space_kw: np.ndarray,
+    dhw_kw: np.ndarray,
+    stop_probability: tuple[float, float],
+    p_max: float,
+    floor: float | None = None,
+) -> float:
+    """The one-row case of :func:`switch_weights_batch`."""
+    return float(switch_weights_batch(
+        np.asarray(space_kw, dtype=float)[None, :], dhw_kw, stop_probability, p_max, floor
+    )[0])
+
+
+def lost_share(
+    stop_probability: tuple[float, float],
+    off_seconds: tuple[float, float],
+    step_minutes: float = PLAN_STEP_MINUTES,
+) -> float:
+    """The share of one step a hot-water to heating stop keeps the compressor off.
+
+    Only that direction carries lost time: its stop shortens the heating leg
+    that follows, and no install has measured an off time the other way.
+    """
+    return min(1.0, stop_probability[0] * off_seconds[0] / (step_minutes * 60.0))
+
+
+def availability(
+    space_start_kw: np.ndarray,
+    dhw_kw: np.ndarray,
+    lost: float,
+    floor: float | None = None,
+) -> np.ndarray | None:
+    """Per step, the share of it the compressor can run after a priced stop.
+
+    One step is charged per hot-water block end: the step holding the heating
+    leg that follows the hot-water leg in ``space_start_kw``, the profile the
+    solve starts from, because which step that is is the solve's own variable.
+    ``None`` when nothing is charged, so the caller makes today's calls on
+    today's arrays instead of multiplying by ones.
+    """
+    if not lost > 0:
+        return None
+    first, last, two = leg_ends(space_start_kw, dhw_kw, floor)
+    charged = two.copy()
+    charged[1:] |= (last[:-1] == DHW) & (first[1:] == SPACE)
+    if not charged.any():
+        return None
+    return np.where(charged, 1.0 - lost, 1.0)
+
+
+def space_headroom(
+    p_max: float, dhw_kw: np.ndarray, avail: np.ndarray | None, floor: float | None
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The space draw a hot-water plan leaves, less a stop's lost running time.
+
+    On a duty-cycle install (no ``floor``) a schedule value is a step average
+    and the stop is part of the off time, so the bound carries it. On a
+    clamped install a value is the level the compressor runs at and the bound
+    is today's; :func:`delivered_space` carries the lost time there.
+    """
+    if avail is None or floor is not None:
+        return np.maximum(0.0, p_max - dhw_kw)
+    charged: np.ndarray = np.maximum(0.0, avail * p_max - dhw_kw)
+    return charged
+
+
+def delivered_space(
+    space_kw: np.ndarray, dhw_kw: np.ndarray, avail: np.ndarray, floor: float | None
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The step average the house receives from a shipped space level.
+
+    On a clamped install the compressor is off for ``1 - avail`` of a step it
+    runs at level ``space + dhw``, and hot water keeps the level its planner
+    booked. On a duty-cycle install the shipped draw is already the average.
+    """
+    if floor is None:
+        return space_kw
+    delivered: np.ndarray = np.maximum(0.0, space_kw - (1.0 - avail) * (space_kw + dhw_kw))
+    return delivered
+
+
+def switch_ban(
+    space_kw: np.ndarray, stop_probability: tuple[float, float], floor: float | None
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The steps hot water may not be placed on to avoid a priced switch.
+
+    For hot water to heating: where heating runs in that step or the next, so
+    a block can only end into a planned stop or into more hot water. For
+    heating to hot water it mirrors onto the previous step.
+    """
+    on = _runs(np.asarray(space_kw, dtype=float), floor)
+    ban = np.zeros(on.shape, dtype=bool)
+    if stop_probability[0] > 0:
+        ban |= on
+        ban[:-1] |= on[1:]
+    if stop_probability[1] > 0:
+        ban |= on
+        ban[1:] |= on[:-1]
+    return ban

+def _priced_stops(opt: HeatPumpOptimizer) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
+    """The learned stop probability per switch direction, ``None`` when no direction stops.
+
+    The lost running time is charged on this alone; the price is this times
+    ``cycling_cost``, so an install that prices no cycle prices no switch.
+    """
+    stops = duty_legs.priced_pair(opt.config.duty_switch_stop_probability, 1.0)
+    return stops if max(stops) > 0 else None
+
+
+def _stop_availability(
+    opt: HeatPumpOptimizer, start: np.ndarray, dhw_plan: np.ndarray, p_max: float
+) -> np.ndarray | None:
+    """The running share a priced stop leaves each step of the profile a solve starts from.
+
+    Read on the levels that profile ships, so the charged step holds a
+    heating leg the arbiter serves. ``None`` unless a stop with a measured off
+    time is priced: the caller then makes today's calls.
+    """
+    stops = _priced_stops(opt)
+    if stops is None:
+        return None
+    lost = duty_legs.lost_share(
+        stops, duty_legs.priced_pair(opt.config.duty_switch_off_seconds)
+    )
+    space, tank = _realize_joint(
+        opt.config.clamp_planned_levels,
+        np.minimum(start, np.maximum(0.0, p_max - dhw_plan)),
+        dhw_plan, opt.model.params.min_electrical_power, p_max,
+    )
+    return duty_legs.availability(space, tank, lost, _duty_floor(opt))
+
+
+def _with_stop_availability(
+    opt: HeatPumpOptimizer,
+    start: np.ndarray,
+    dhw_plan: np.ndarray,
+    p_max: float,
+    objective: Callable[..., float],
+    objective_batch: Callable[..., np.ndarray],
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, Callable[..., float], Callable[..., np.ndarray]]:
+    """What a priced stop changes about one space solve: its bound and its objectives.
+
+    The heat pump serves one circuit at a time, so a DHW block eats into the
+    capacity available for space heating during that step, and a stop after
+    it into the step that follows. The availability vector is constant for
+    the solve and is kept on the optimizer beside the requirement, so the
+    plan that is adopted publishes with the vector it was scored with. With
+    none, the bound is ``p_max - dhw`` and the objectives the ones handed in.
+    """
+    avail = opt._space_avail = _stop_availability(opt, start, dhw_plan, p_max)
+    headroom = duty_legs.space_headroom(p_max, dhw_plan, avail, _duty_floor(opt))
+    if avail is None:
+        return headroom, objective, objective_batch
+    return headroom, partial(objective, avail=avail), partial(objective_batch, avail=avail)
+
+
+def _shipped_and_received(
+    opt: HeatPumpOptimizer,
+    space: np.ndarray,
+    dhw: np.ndarray | None,
+    avail: np.ndarray | None,
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray | None, np.ndarray]:
+    """The level each circuit ships at, and the space draw the house receives.
+
+    The two differ only where a priced stop keeps the compressor off for part
+    of a step (``duty_legs.delivered_space``); with no availability vector the
+    received draw is the shipped array itself, the same object. A relaxed
+    start of a clamped install gets the clamped reading on its unrounded
+    level: the stop is the install's, whatever the rounding.
+    """
+    space, dhw = _realize_draw(
+        _scores_rounded(opt), space, dhw,

+    )
+    if avail is None or dhw is None:
+        return space, dhw, space
+    return space, dhw, duty_legs.delivered_space(space, dhw, avail, _duty_floor(opt))
+
+
+def _switch_cost_fn(
+    opt: HeatPumpOptimizer,
+) -> Callable[[np.ndarray, np.ndarray | None], Any]:
+    """The duty-switch term of shipped plans, beside the cycling term.
+
+    One entry per row of a ``[B, n]`` batch, a float for one plan: the
+    one-row case of the same reduction, so the two agree bit for bit.
+    ``None`` when no direction is priced or there is no hot-water plan, and
+    :func:`_with_switch_cost` then adds no operand at all.
+    """
+    stops, floor = _priced_stops(opt), _duty_floor(opt)
+    p_max, cost = opt.model.params.max_electrical_power, opt.config.cycling_cost
+
+    def switch_cost(space: np.ndarray, dhw: np.ndarray | None) -> Any:
+        if stops is None or dhw is None or not cost > 0:
+            return None
+        term = cost * duty_legs.switch_weights_batch(
+            np.atleast_2d(space), dhw, stops, p_max, floor)
+        return term if np.ndim(space) == 2 else float(term[0])
+
+    return switch_cost
+
+
+def _with_switch_cost(level_cost: Any, switch_cost: Any) -> Any:
+    """The cycling and capacity terms plus the duty-switch term, when there is one."""
+    return level_cost if switch_cost is None else level_cost + switch_cost
+
+
+def _dhw_build(
+    planner: DhwPlanner, h: _Horizon, p_max: float, **extra: Any
+) -> tuple[Any, np.ndarray]:
+    """One hot-water build, with what every pass of a solve hands the planner.
+
+    The block honours an external ceiling through one scalar, the horizon's
+    minimum -- the same conservative, never-over-the-line approximation the
+    fuse guard's cap already makes. A quiet silent window's cap therefore
+    bounds every block the same way (#1910); its OFF steps are per-step,
+    through the forced-off door where the energy is re-bought elsewhere. The
+    mode's block rides every build (#1747): a replan without it plans hot
+    water the mode cannot make, and masks the breach.
+    """
+    return planner._build_dhw_requirements(
+        h,
+        p_max=p_max,
+        p_run_cap=(
+            float(np.min(h.power_caps_extra))

+            else None
+        ),
+        blocked=h.dhw_blocked,
+        off_steps=h.off_steps,
+        **extra,
+    )
+
+
+def _avoid_priced_switches(
+    opt: HeatPumpOptimizer,
+    h: _Horizon,
+    planner: DhwPlanner,
+    solve_space: Callable[..., Any],
+    objective: Callable[..., float],
+    p_max: float,
+    incumbent: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, str],
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, str]:
+    """Try one hot-water plan placed where no priced switch follows it.
+
+    Where the block sits is combinatorial, so it is taken by candidate and
+    score, as ``_co_optimize`` takes its own: hot water is banned from the
+    steps whose heating would make the switch, and the plan is adopted only
+    if it scores lower on the same objective, keeps off every banned step a
+    manual pin does not force on, and holds its own requirement wherever the
+    incumbent holds its. A refused candidate leaves the incumbent's
+    requirement and availability in place. Not on a combi store, whose
+    hot-water plan is a feasibility repair and never a scored candidate.
+    """
+    space, dhw, _ = incumbent

+    if stops is None or not opt.config.cycling_cost > 0 or opt.model.params.dhw_store.combi:
+        return incumbent
+    floor = _duty_floor(opt)
+    shipped, tank = _realize_joint(
+        opt.config.clamp_planned_levels, space, dhw,
+        opt.model.params.min_electrical_power, p_max,
+    )
+    kept_avail, kept_requirement = opt._space_avail, opt._dhw_requirement
+    if kept_requirement is None or not duty_legs.switch_weight(shipped, tank, stops, p_max, floor) > 0:
+        return incumbent
+    try:
+        ban = duty_legs.switch_ban(shipped, stops, floor)
+        plan, requirement = _dhw_build(
+            planner, h, p_max,
+            wood_temps=planner._dhw_coil_wood_forecast(h), placement_ban=ban,
+        )
+        forced_on = (
+            np.zeros(ban.shape, dtype=bool) if h.dhw_pins is None
+            else np.nan_to_num(_padded(h.dhw_pins, ban.size)) >= 0.5
+        )
+
+        def first_short(
+            schedule: np.ndarray, floor_temps: np.ndarray, excused: set[int]
+        ) -> tuple[Any, int | None]:
+            """The planner's own tank walk and shortfall rule, past ``excused`` steps."""
+            temps, _, step = planner._dhw_shortfall(
+                temps_of.get(id(schedule)), schedule, h.initial_state.dhw_temperature,
+                h.outdoor_temps, plan.draw_rates, h.dt, h.humidity, floor_temps, excused,
+            )
+            temps_of[id(schedule)] = temps
+            return temps, step

+        # The steps the incumbent is itself short on excuse the candidate there.
+        temps_of: dict[int, Any] = {}
+        unheld: set[int] = set()
+        while (step := first_short(dhw, kept_requirement, unheld)[1]) is not None:
+            unheld.add(step)
+        if (
+            not np.any(plan.schedule[ban & ~forced_on] > 0)
+            and first_short(plan.schedule, requirement, unheld)[1] is None
+        ):

+            candidate_space, candidate_status, score = solve_space(plan.schedule, space)
+            if score < base - 1e-9:

+                return candidate_space, plan.schedule, candidate_status
+    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - a candidate is optional: the incumbent stands
+        _LOGGER.debug("Duty-switch candidate pass skipped: %s", err)
+    opt._space_avail = kept_avail
+    return incumbent
+
+

+    "detector": "merge_train.py --self-test: _gate_reader_barrier_self_test drives PLANTED_READERS (a direct call, an import alias, a rebinding, getattr, functools.partial, a *self_test* name, no busy, a literal (), an unminted empty Busy) from four modules and fails unless each read raises; and fails on merge_pr.sh reading its raw red without the classify wait",
+    "detector_idea": null,
+    "barrier": "merge_train.classify judges its own callers at run time: busy is required and must be a Busy (an empty one minted only by the BUSY_MINTERS run readers) or FINAL from a FINAL_READERS frame (repo path, co_qualname), else BlindRead -- whatever spelling reached the call; policy_refusal reads same-named gate contexts together. Not covered: a read of a gate conclusion that never calls classify, and an empty Busy minted by gate_busy over fabricated runs",
+    "status": "barriered",
+    "nearest_existing": "N-postreview-merge-red",
+    "mechanism_difference": "The writer's meaning changed (a deferral became a routine red) and the readers did not; the failure is a read-side classification, not a merge of a reviewed head.",
+    "aliases": [
+      "a provisional gate red read as final"
+    ],
+    "non_round_note": "Process defect from triage batch 136 (P436); instances: #3264 review run 42436586762 (red 02:01:18Z, sibling green 02:01:51Z), and the 2026-11-12 03:20-04:45Z heads of #3479, #3454, #3442 and #3465. Not an audit finding, not counted in total.",
+    "non_round_instances": [
+      "#3264 review run 42436586762",
+      "#3479",
+      "#3454",
+      "#3442",
+      "#3465"
+    ],
+    "rca": [
+      "R10-RCA-GATE-DEFER-READ-FINAL"
+    ],
+    "rca_planned": [],
+    "trigger": {
+      "per_round": false,
+      "cross_round": false,
+      "barriered_any": false,
+      "class_rca_on_record": false
+    }
   }
-}
+}

diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_duty_switch_price_section.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_duty_switch_price_section.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..6f6895aca6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_duty_switch_price_section.py
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Run R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE's section of ``tests/features.py`` alone, and its mutants.
+
+WHY IT EXISTS. ``tests/features.py`` has no section filter, and the mutation
+proof of the group (the leg rule's leaf, the switch term, the lost running
+time, the banned candidate, the learner's count cap and its read for the
+planner) runs the section once per mutant. This cuts the section out of the
+script at its two markers, binds the six names the script had bound by then,
+and runs it. It executes the tree's own text: a check edited in
+``tests/features.py`` is the check run here.
+
+It refuses (exit 2) when a marker is missing or the section holds no check,
+so a moved marker cannot read as a pass.
+
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_duty_switch_price_section.py
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_duty_switch_price_section.py --mutants [name ...]
+
+``--mutants`` copies the package and ``tests/`` to a private directory per
+mutant, applies one edit there (the tree is never written), runs the section
+on the copy and prints the checks that went red. An unmutated copy runs
+first as the control and must pass. A mutant whose pattern is not found
+exactly once, or that turns no check red, is printed as such and the exit
+code is 1. The coordinator's one argument is outside the section (its check
+sits beside #1512's in the lifecycle part of the script) and is proven by a
+whole run of ``tests/features.py``.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def repo_root(start):
+    """The directory holding custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+    here = Path(start).resolve()
+    if here.is_file():
+        here = here.parent
+    marker = Path("custom_components") / "heatpump_optimizer" / "manifest.json"
+    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
+        if (cand / marker).is_file():
+            return cand
+    raise RuntimeError(f"no repository root above {start}")
+
+
+ROOT = repo_root(os.environ.get("DSP_SECTION_ROOT") or __file__)
+START = "from types import SimpleNamespace as _DspNS"
+END = '\nsys.exit(R.close("FEATURE CHECKS"))'
+PRELUDE = """
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+import numpy as np
+from harness import Results, UTC
+from profiles import solve_inputs
+R = Results("R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE's section of tests/features.py")
+"""
+PKG = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/"
+
+#: name, file, the text to find exactly once, its replacement.
+MUTANTS: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = [
+    ("optimizer: a candidate is tried with no requirement to hold it to", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "if kept_requirement is None or not duty_legs.switch_weight(", "if not duty_legs.switch_weight("),
+    ("optimizer: a candidate pass that raises is not caught", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - a candidate is optional", "    except KeyError as err:  # a candidate is optional"),
+    ("learner: no count cap", PKG + "duty_switch.py",
+     "        if self.n > N_CAP:\n", "        if False:\n"),
+    ("learner: the cap scales the stops alone", PKG + "duty_switch.py",
+     "self.k, self.kept_w = self.k * scale, self.kept_w * scale", "self.k = self.k * scale"),
+    ("learner: the cap is three times the on-threshold", PKG + "duty_switch.py",
+     "N_CAP = 2.0 * N_ON", "N_CAP = 3.0 * N_ON"),
+    ("learner: the read ignores the latch", PKG + "duty_switch.py",
+     "read = [d if d.usable else Direction() for", "read = [d for"),
+    ("learner: the read swaps the directions", PKG + "duty_switch.py",
+     "return (read[0].p, read[1].p), (read[0].median_off_s or 0.0, read[1].median_off_s or 0.0)",
+     "return (read[1].p, read[0].p), (read[1].median_off_s or 0.0, read[0].median_off_s or 0.0)"),
+    ("learner: the read hands the off time of the other direction", PKG + "duty_switch.py",
+     "(read[0].median_off_s or 0.0, read[1].median_off_s or 0.0)",
+     "(read[1].median_off_s or 0.0, read[0].median_off_s or 0.0)"),
+    ("leaf: the hot-water-to-heating switch reads the other direction", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "(before == DHW) & (after == SPACE),\n        p_ds,", "(before == DHW) & (after == SPACE),\n        p_sd,"),
+    ("leaf: the switch weight takes the larger neighbouring draw", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "np.minimum(level[_BEFORE], level[_AFTER])", "np.maximum(level[_BEFORE], level[_AFTER])"),
+    ("leaf: the in-step weight draws the smaller circuit, not the combined draw", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "np.where(two, p_ds * level, 0.0)",
+     "np.where(two, p_ds * np.minimum(space, np.asarray(dhw_kw, dtype=float)), 0.0)"),
+    ("leaf: the weight is not divided by the maximum draw", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "axis=1)) / p_max", "axis=1))"),
+    ("leaf: a small hot-water share no longer collapses to heating", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "to_space = both & (dhw_min < SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES)", "to_space = both & (dhw_min > SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES)"),
+    ("leaf: a small heating share no longer collapses to hot water", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "~to_space & (step_minutes - dhw_min < SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES)",
+     "~to_space & (step_minutes - dhw_min > SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES)"),
+    ("leaf: the leg classification ignores the duty floor", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "_runs(space, floor), _runs(dhw, floor)", "_runs(space, None), _runs(dhw, None)"),
+    # The leaf has no zero-pair return: zero probabilities weigh zero on the
+    # full path, and the optimizer never calls it without a priced direction.
+    ("leaf: a pump with no maximum draw is not returned early", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "    if p_max <= 0:\n        return np.zeros(space.shape[0])", "    if p_max < 0:\n        return np.zeros(space.shape[0])"),
+    ("leaf: a negative learned value is kept", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "max(v, 0.0) if math.isfinite(v) and v <= upper", "v if math.isfinite(v) and v <= upper"),
+    ("leaf: a learned value on its upper bound reads as zero", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "max(v, 0.0) if math.isfinite(v) and v <= upper", "max(v, 0.0) if math.isfinite(v) and v < upper"),
+    ("leaf: the early return is one entry per step, not per row", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "return np.zeros(space.shape[0])", "return np.zeros(space.shape[1])"),
+    ("optimizer: no priced direction still returns a pair", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "return stops if max(stops) > 0 else None", "return stops"),
+    ("leaf: the charged step is the hot-water block's last step", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "charged[1:] |= (last[:-1] == DHW) & (first[1:] == SPACE)",
+     "charged[:-1] |= (last[:-1] == DHW) & (first[1:] == SPACE)"),
+    ("leaf: the delivered draw is keyed on the clamped install", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "    if floor is None:\n        return space_kw", "    if floor is not None:\n        return space_kw"),
+    ("leaf: the delivered draw loses only the space share", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "(1.0 - avail) * (space_kw + dhw_kw)", "(1.0 - avail) * space_kw"),
+    ("optimizer: the switch term is handed the delivered draw", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "switch_cost(space_power, dhw_plan_power)", "switch_cost(heat_power, dhw_plan_power)"),
+    ("optimizer: the simulation is handed the shipped draw", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "_space_traj(heat_power, buffer_exo_kw)", "_space_traj(space_power, buffer_exo_kw)"),
+    ("optimizer: the energy cost is handed the shipped draw", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "drawn = combined if heat_power is space_power else heat_power + dhw_plan_power",
+     "drawn = combined"),
+    ("optimizer: the publication drops the solve's availability vector", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "heat_space = optimal_space if self._space_avail is None else duty_legs",
+     "heat_space = optimal_space if True else duty_legs"),
+    ("planner: the placement ban is not OR'd into forced_off", PKG + "dhw_planner.py",
+     "return forced_off if ban is None else _forced_off_with(forced_off, ban, n_steps)",
+     "return forced_off"),
+    ("optimizer: a candidate short of its requirement is adopted", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "            and first_short(plan.schedule, requirement, unheld)[1] is None\n",
+     "            and True\n"),
+    ("optimizer: a candidate with hot water on a banned step is adopted", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "            not np.any(plan.schedule[ban & ~forced_on] > 0)\n", "            True\n"),
+    ("optimizer: the candidate is adopted on a higher score", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "if score < base - 1e-9:", "if score > base - 1e-9:"),
+    ("leaf: the lost share is not capped at one", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "return min(1.0, stop_probability[0] * off_seconds[0] / (step_minutes * 60.0))",
+     "return stop_probability[0] * off_seconds[0] / (step_minutes * 60.0)"),
+    ("leaf: the lost share ignores the stop probability", PKG + "duty_legs.py",
+     "min(1.0, stop_probability[0] * off_seconds[0] /", "min(1.0, off_seconds[0] /"),
+    # The fix reviewer's three survivors at ee89d50b2b (R5, R9, R11), its texts.
+    ("optimizer: the co-optimisation headroom ignores the availability vector", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "p_max, dhw_power, self._space_avail, _duty_floor(self))", "p_max, dhw_power, None, _duty_floor(self))"),
+    ("optimizer: the availability vector is classified with no duty floor", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "return duty_legs.availability(space, tank, lost, _duty_floor(opt))",
+     "return duty_legs.availability(space, tank, lost, None)"),
+    ("optimizer: the candidate pass runs on a combi store", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "or not opt.config.cycling_cost > 0 or opt.model.params.dhw_store.combi:",
+     "or not opt.config.cycling_cost > 0:"),
+    ("optimizer: the co-optimisation headroom is handed no duty floor", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "p_max, dhw_power, self._space_avail, _duty_floor(self))", "p_max, dhw_power, self._space_avail, None)"),
+    # Repair round 2: the two clamps left on the line the availability reads
+    # its start through, the mutation table's CLAMP_DROP twins of one anchor.
+    ("optimizer: the start is read with no cap beside hot water", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "np.minimum(start, np.maximum(0.0, p_max - dhw_plan)),", "(start),"),
+    ("optimizer: the start is capped at zero in every step", PKG + "optimizer.py",
+     "np.minimum(start, np.maximum(0.0, p_max - dhw_plan)),", "np.minimum(start, (0.0)),"),
+    ("arbiter: the share serves the legs in reverse order", PKG + "pump_arbiter.py",
+     "return legs[0][0] if (now - result.timestamps[i]) < first_ends else legs[-1][0]",
+     "return legs[-1][0] if (now - result.timestamps[i]) < first_ends else legs[0][0]"),
+]
+
+
+def run_section(root: Path) -> int:
+    text = (root / "tests" / "features.py").read_text()
+    if text.count(START) != 1 or text.count(END) != 1:
+        print("REFUSED: a section marker is missing or repeated in tests/features.py")
+        return 2
+    section = text[text.index(START):text.index(END)]
+    sys.path[:0] = [str(root / "tests"), str(root / "custom_components")]
+    scope: dict = {"__name__": "duty_switch_price_section"}
+    exec(compile(PRELUDE + section, "tests/features.py[duty-switch-price]", "exec"), scope)
+    results = scope["R"]
+    if not results.checks:
+        print("REFUSED: the section ran no check")
+        return 2
+    return results.close("DUTY-SWITCH PLANNER-PRICE SECTION CHECKS")
+
+
+def _copy_run(edit: tuple[str, str, str] | None) -> tuple[int | None, list[str]]:
+    """The section's exit code and red check names on a private copy, ``None`` when the pattern is not there once."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        copy = Path(tmp)
+        for part in ("custom_components", "tests"):
+            shutil.copytree(ROOT / part, copy / part, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "golden"))
+        if edit is not None:
+            path, old, new = edit
+            text = (copy / path).read_text()
+            if text.count(old) != 1:
+                return None, []
+            (copy / path).write_text(text.replace(old, new))
+        env = {**os.environ, "DSP_SECTION_ROOT": str(copy / "custom_components"),
+               "PYTHONPATH": str(copy / "tests" / "hastub"), "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"}
+        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__], cwd=copy, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
+        red = [line[7:].split("  [")[0] for line in out.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("  FAIL ")]
+        if "SECTION CHECKS" not in out.stdout:  # a traceback exits 1 too, and closes nothing
+            red.append(f"the section stopped: {(out.stderr.strip().splitlines() or ['no output'])[-1]}")
+        return out.returncode, red
+
+
+def run_mutants(names: list[str]) -> int:
+    code, red = _copy_run(None)
+    print(f"== control, no edit: exit {code}, {len(red)} red")
+    if code != 0:
+        print("\n".join(f"     {name}" for name in red))
+        return 1
+    bad = 0
+    for name, path, old, new in MUTANTS:
+        if names and name not in names:
+            continue
+        code, red = _copy_run((path, old, new))
+        verdict = "PATTERN NOT FOUND ONCE" if code is None else f"{len(red)} red" if red else "SURVIVED"
+        bad += not red
+        print(f"== {name}: {verdict}")
+        print("\n".join(f"     {check}" for check in red), end="\n" if red else "")
+    print(f"RESULT mutants_not_killed={bad}")
+    return 1 if bad else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    os.chdir(ROOT)
+    sys.exit(run_mutants(sys.argv[2:]) if sys.argv[1:2] == ["--mutants"] else run_section(ROOT))
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..7b3c9bbce6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier.py
@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER: the finder's harness for two readers of a deferral gate red.
+
+    python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier.py [--tree DIR]
+
+DIR is a tree root holding tools/audit/seat/ (merge_train.py, gh_read.py) and tools/ci/gate.py (default:
+this tree). To measure a baseline, export it first:
+
+    git archive <sha> tools/audit/seat tools/ci | tar -x -C "$D" && python3 -I ... --tree "$D"
+
+Arms, each driving the tree's own Train with a fake `gh` (no network):
+  policy   #3264's review instance: the rollup holds a passing `gate` (a CI review
+           run's) and a failing `gate` (the edit run's deferral). policy_refusal
+           must be a wait (second field True), not the park "the missing requirement
+           is a review". Null: a rollup of the passing gate alone is the park as before.
+  policy-real-red / policy-hidden-red   a real gate red beside an unrelated unfinished workflow, and another
+           required context's red beside a deferral gate, must both read red (no wait, the context named).
+  under    #3398's shape: a deferral red whose code run is in_progress, started and
+           inside its deadline, outlives `polls`; wait_ci must return [] once the run
+           ends, not ["TIMEOUT"]. Null: a QUEUED run keeps the polls bound (TIMEOUT).
+A line `DEFECT <arm>` is printed per arm that reads the defect, then RESULT lines;
+the exit code is 1 when any DEFECT stands, 0 otherwise.
+"""
+import argparse
+import datetime
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def load(tree: Path):
+    seat = tree / "tools/audit/seat"
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(seat))
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("mt_under_test", str(seat / "merge_train.py"))
+    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules["mt_under_test"] = mod
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    return mod
+
+
+def policy(mt, rollup, ci=(), every=(), req=("gate",)):
+    H, NOW = "b" * 40, 1_000_000.0
+
+    def run(argv, cwd=None, stdin=None):
+        a = " ".join(argv)
+        if "workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=" in a:
+            return 0, "".join(json.dumps(x) + "\n" for x in ci)
+        if "actions/runs?head_sha=" in a:
+            return 0, "".join(json.dumps(x) + "\n" for x in every)
+        if "actions/runs?event=pull_request_review" in a:
+            return 0, ""
+        if "statusCheckRollup" in a:
+            return 0, json.dumps({"mergeStateStatus": "BLOCKED", "reviewDecision": "APPROVED",
+                                  "statusCheckRollup": [r if isinstance(r, dict) else {"name": "gate", "conclusion": r}
+                                                        for r in rollup]})
+        if "/reviews" in a:
+            return 0, json.dumps([[]])
+        return 0, ""
+    t = mt.Train("o/r", Path("."), None, "", (), 1, run=run, sleep=lambda s: None, log=lambda s: None,
+                 polls=3, wall=lambda: NOW)
+    t.required = lambda pr_head=False: list(req)
+    return t.policy_refusal(3264, H)
+
+
+def under(mt, status, polls=3):
+    NOW = 1_800_000_000.0
+    started = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(NOW - 5000, datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
+    gate = {"name": "gate", "status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure", "started_at": "2026-11-06T14:55:00Z",
+            "id": 1, "check_suite": {"id": 11}}
+    green = dict(gate, conclusion="success", started_at="2026-11-06T15:26:00Z", id=3)
+    seen = [0, 0]
+
+    def run(argv, cwd=None, stdin=None):
+        a = " ".join(argv)
+        if "check-runs" in a:
+            cur = [gate] if seen[0] < 8 else [green]
+            seen[0] += 1
+            return 0, "\n".join(json.dumps(c) for c in cur)
+        if "actions/runs?head_sha=" in a:
+            seen[1] += 1
+            # the paged read's answer: one JSON object per line (`--jq .[]`), as merge_train.py's `pages` reads it
+            row = ({"id": 42237558473, "status": status, "run_started_at": started} if seen[1] <= 7
+                   else {"id": 42237558473, "status": "completed", "run_started_at": ""})
+            return 0, json.dumps(row) + "\n"
+        return 0, ""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
+        t = mt.Train("o/r", Path(d), None, "", (), 1, run=run, sleep=lambda s: None, log=lambda s: None,
+                     polls=polls, wall=lambda: NOW)
+        return t.wait_ci("e" * 40, only=["gate"])
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--tree", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]))
+    mt = load(Path(ap.parse_args().tree))
+    defects = 0
+    got = policy(mt, ["SUCCESS", "FAILURE"])
+    bad = not (got[1] is True and "review" not in got[0].split("(")[0])
+    got0 = policy(mt, ["SUCCESS"])
+    print(f"RESULT policy_wait={got[1]} policy_text_names_review={'review' in got[0].split('(')[0]}")
+    print(f"RESULT policy_null_waits={got0[1]} (the passing gate alone must not wait)")
+    print(f"RESULT policy_null_ok={got0[1] is False}")
+    if bad:
+        print("DEFECT policy"); defects += 1
+    if got0[1] is not False:
+        print("DEFECT policy-null"); defects += 1
+    # a real red is never read as a deferral (the round-2 verdict's cases): the arm's DEFECT is a wait, or a hidden red
+    fail = lambda n, at: {"name": n, "conclusion": "FAILURE", "completedAt": at}  # noqa: E731
+    other = [{"id": 9, "name": "codeql", "status": "in_progress"}]
+    code = [{"id": 5, "status": "queued"}]
+    fast = "tests / fast (3.14)"
+    b = policy(mt, [fail("gate", "2026-11-12T09:55:00Z"), fail("gate", "2026-11-12T11:00:00Z")], every=other)
+    c = policy(mt, [fail("gate", "2026-11-12T09:55:00Z"), fail(fast, "2026-11-12T10:10:00Z")], ci=code, req=("gate", fast))
+    a = policy(mt, [fail("gate", "2026-11-12T09:55:00Z")], ci=code)
+    print(f"RESULT policy_B_wait={b[1]} policy_C_wait={c[1]} policy_C_names_fast={fast in c[0]} policy_A_wait={a[1]}")
+    if b[1] is not False:
+        print("DEFECT policy-real-red"); defects += 1
+    if c[1] is not False or fast not in c[0]:
+        print("DEFECT policy-hidden-red"); defects += 1
+    r = under(mt, "in_progress")
+    q = under(mt, "queued")
+    print(f"RESULT under_started={r} under_queued_null={q}")
+    if r != []:
+        print("DEFECT under"); defects += 1
+    if q != ["TIMEOUT"]:
+        print("DEFECT under-null"); defects += 1
+    return 1 if defects else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier_mutants.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier_mutants.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..2d0c9fb19e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier_mutants.py
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER: mutants of the deferral barrier in merge_train.classify.
+
+    python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_barrier_mutants.py [--tree DIR] [--plants-only]
+
+DIR is a tree root holding tools/audit/seat/ and tools/ci/ (default: this tree); a baseline is measured by
+exporting it first (`git archive <sha> tools/audit/seat tools/ci | tar -x -C "$D"`, then `--tree "$D"`).
+
+Two arms. PLANT: one deferral-blind reader per shape the fourth blocked verdict named (import alias,
+rebinding, getattr, functools.partial, a function named *self_test*, a module outside the four the
+old scan read), each planted into a copy of DIR -- appended to tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, or as
+custom_components/elsewhere.py for the outside module -- and driven on a red `gate`. A plant passes
+FINAL where DIR has it, else no busy (DIR's own blind spelling). It is KILLED when the read raises or
+DIR's `_gate_reader_barrier_self_test`, loaded from the copy, fails a check; SURVIVED when it returns
+a verdict and the block is green. SOURCE (skipped by --plants-only): each row of SOURCE_MUTANTS
+replaces one fragment of merge_train.py that must occur exactly once (else STALE, a failure), and the
+block runs over the mutated source compiled in memory under the file's path; the unmutated source
+is the null control and must fail nothing.
+A line per mutant, then `RESULT plants=N survived=S` and `RESULT mutants=N survived=S stale=T
+baseline_failed=F`; exit 1 unless every count but N is 0.
+"""
+import argparse
+import shutil
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_F = "_F = (FINAL,) if 'FINAL' in globals() else ()\n"
+PLANTS = [
+    ("import alias", "merge_train.py",
+     "def _planted(latest, required):\n    from merge_train import classify as judge\n    return judge(latest, required, *_F)\n"),
+    ("rebinding", "merge_train.py", "_judge = classify\ndef _planted(latest, required):\n    return _judge(latest, required, *_F)\n"),
+    ("getattr", "merge_train.py",
+     "def _planted(latest, required):\n    return getattr(sys.modules['merge_train'], 'classify')(latest, required, *_F)\n"),
+    ("functools.partial", "merge_train.py",
+     "def _planted(latest, required):\n    return functools.partial(classify, latest, required)(*_F)\n"),
+    ("a function named *self_test*", "merge_train.py",
+     "def _planted_self_test(latest, required):\n    return classify(latest, required, *_F)\n_planted = _planted_self_test\n"),
+    ("a module outside the four", "../../../custom_components/elsewhere.py",
+     "def _planted(latest, required):\n    return classify(latest, required, *_F)\n"),
+]
+
+SOURCE_MUTANTS = [
+    ("FINAL accepted from any frame", "elif busy is FINAL and caller_frame(1) in FINAL_READERS:", "elif busy is FINAL:"),
+    ("any value accepted as busy (None, (), a list)", "    if isinstance(busy, Busy):\n        deferred",
+     "    if isinstance(busy, (Busy, list, tuple, type(None))):\n        deferred"),
+    ("an empty Busy minted anywhere", "if not self and caller_frame(1) not in BUSY_MINTERS:", "if False:"),
+    ("FINAL frame read one level too shallow (classify itself)", "elif busy is FINAL and caller_frame(1) in FINAL_READERS:",
+     "elif busy is FINAL and caller_frame(0) in FINAL_READERS:"),
+    ("frames keyed by basename, not repo path", "return rel, code.co_qualname",
+     "return 'tools/audit/seat/' + Path(rel).name, code.co_qualname"),
+    ("frames keyed by path only", "return rel, code.co_qualname", "return rel, 'approval_owed'"),
+]
+
+
+def load(path: Path, source: str, name: str = "merge_train"):
+    mod = types.ModuleType(name)
+    mod.__file__ = str(path)
+    sys.modules[name] = mod
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(path.parent))
+    try:
+        exec(compile(source, str(path), "exec"), mod.__dict__)
+    finally:
+        sys.path.remove(str(path.parent))
+    return mod
+
+
+def block(mod) -> list:
+    failed = []
+    try:
+        mod._gate_reader_barrier_self_test(lambda name, ok: None if ok else failed.append(name))
+    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  a crash of the block is a failure of the block
+        failed.append(f"raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
+    return failed
+
+
+def plant(tree: Path, where: str, src: str) -> str:
+    """'KILLED <why>' or 'SURVIVED <verdict>' for one plant in a copy of <tree>."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
+        for sub in ("tools/audit/seat", "tools/ci"):
+            shutil.copytree(tree / sub, Path(d) / sub)
+        seat = Path(d) / "tools/audit/seat"
+        target = (seat / where).resolve()
+        mt_src = (seat / "merge_train.py").read_text()
+        if where == "merge_train.py":
+            mt_src += "\n" + _F + src
+            (seat / "merge_train.py").write_text(mt_src)
+        else:
+            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            target.write_text(_F + src)
+        mod = load(seat / "merge_train.py", mt_src)
+        if where == "merge_train.py":
+            reader = mod._planted
+        else:
+            ns = {k: v for k, v in mod.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith("__")}
+            exec(compile(target.read_text(), str(target), "exec"), ns)
+            reader = ns["_planted"]
+        red = mod.latest_runs([{"name": mod.GATE, "status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure", "started_at": "1"}])
+        try:
+            got = reader(red, [mod.GATE])
+        except TypeError as e:
+            return f"KILLED   read refused: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:70]}"
+        failed = block(mod)
+        return f"KILLED   block: {failed[0][:70]}" if failed else f"SURVIVED read {got[0]}, block green"
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--tree", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]))
+    ap.add_argument("--plants-only", action="store_true")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    tree = Path(args.tree).resolve()
+    survived = 0
+    for name, where, src in PLANTS:
+        line = plant(tree, where, src)
+        survived += line.startswith("SURVIVED")
+        print(f"PLANT {name}: {line}")
+    print(f"RESULT plants={len(PLANTS)} survived={survived}")
+    if args.plants_only:
+        return 1 if survived else 0
+    path = tree / "tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py"
+    src = path.read_text()
+    base = block(load(path, src))
+    print(f"BASELINE failed={len(base)} {base[:2]}")
+    msurv = stale = 0
+    for name, old, new in SOURCE_MUTANTS:
+        if src.count(old) != 1:
+            stale += 1
+            print(f"STALE    {name} (fragment occurs {src.count(old)} times)")
+            continue
+        failed = block(load(path, src.replace(old, new)))
+        msurv += not failed
+        print(f"{'KILLED  ' if failed else 'SURVIVED'} {name} | {failed[0][:80] if failed else '-'} (+{max(len(failed) - 1, 0)})")
+    print(f"RESULT mutants={len(SOURCE_MUTANTS)} survived={msurv} stale={stale} baseline_failed={len(base)}")
+    return 1 if survived or msurv or stale or base else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_4.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_4.py

     crs, runs = as_of(fx["3293"], ts("2026-11-07T21:07:00Z"))
     crs = crs + [unit("fast", 99, conclusion="failure")]
     req = ["fast"]
-    st = (mt.classify(mt.latest_runs(crs), req))[0].upper()
+    idle = (mt.gate_busy([], []),) if hasattr(mt, "Busy") else ()  # a tree whose classify requires busy: none at this head

     print(f"SCENE null-red-non-gate want=RED got={st}")
     bad += st != "RED"
     print(f"RESULT replay defects={defects} settle_gap={gap} null_bad={bad} scenes={len(rows) + 1}")
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_held_capacity_census.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_held_capacity_census.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..5b597dec0c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_held_capacity_census.py
@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+"""R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: the held state's census over every bound on the reference's heat.
+
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components \\
+        python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_held_capacity_census.py
+
+Drives ``_thermostat_held_state`` over a grid of installs -- no valve and the
+three throttling valve modes, both zonings, the derived and the
+``two_tank_4way`` layout, pumps of 4, 6 and 9 kW, valve targets 21 to 40 C,
+outdoor -25 to 18 C -- and books one reference step from each held state at
+``_compute_baseline_power``'s power on a one-step horizon (nothing to
+apportion). The property is the phenomenon's, not an instance's: a held state
+the reference step can keep draws no stored heat on its first booked step.
+Prints the case count, the worst first-step store change in kWh_th and the
+count over 0.02 kWh_th, then the capacity control: at -25 C a 9 kW pump holds
+21 C (valved and not), a 4 kW pump does not.
+
+Preconditions, asserted (exit 1): every grid case ran without an exception,
+every held room lies in [min(outdoor, 21), 21], and the case count is the
+grid's product.
+"""
+
+import itertools
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from heatpump_optimizer.optimizer import (
+    HeatPumpOptimizer,
+    OptimizationConfig,
+    _thermostat_held_state,
+)
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import (
+    ThermalModel,
+    ThermalParameters,
+    ThermalState,
+    WeatherSeries,
+)
+from profiles import house
+
+TARGET_C = 21.0
+MODES = ("none", "manual", "smart_read", "smart_write")
+ZONINGS = (True, False)
+LAYOUTS = (None, "two_tank_4way")
+PUMPS_KW = (4.0, 6.0, 9.0)
+VALVE_TARGETS_C = (21.0, 25.0, 30.0, 40.0)
+OUTDOORS_C = (-25.0, -15.0, -5.0, 0.0, 5.0, 10.0, 14.0, 16.0, 18.0)
+
+
+def first_step(mode, two_zone, layout, pump_kw, valve_target, outdoor):
+    """The held state and its first booked reference step's store change, kWh_th."""
+    cfg = {"buffer_tank_volume": 750.0, "buffer_max_temperature": 56.0,
+           "heat_pump_max_power": pump_kw}
+    if mode != "none":
+        cfg.update(mixing_valve_mode=mode, mixing_valve_target=valve_target)
+    if layout:
+        cfg["topology_layout"] = layout
+    model = ThermalModel(ThermalParameters.from_config(house(two_zone=two_zone, dhw=False, **cfg)))
+    opt = HeatPumpOptimizer(model, OptimizationConfig(
+        horizon_hours=1, time_step_minutes=15, target_temp=TARGET_C))
+    weather = WeatherSeries(outdoor_temps=np.array([outdoor]), wind_speeds=np.zeros(1),
+                            precipitation=np.zeros(1), solar_radiation=np.zeros(1))
+    start = ThermalState(room_temperature=20.5, slab_temperature=22.0,
+                         outdoor_temperature=outdoor, upper_floor_temperature=20.5,
+                         lower_floor_temperature=20.5, buffer_tank_temperature=30.0)
+    held = _thermostat_held_state(model, start, weather, TARGET_C)
+    power = float(opt._compute_baseline_power(weather, start, 0.25)[0][0])
+    nxt = model.simulate_step(held, power, outdoor, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.25)
+    return held, opt._stored_thermal_energy(nxt) - opt._stored_thermal_energy(held), power
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    grid = list(itertools.product(MODES, ZONINGS, LAYOUTS, PUMPS_KW, VALVE_TARGETS_C, OUTDOORS_C))
+    ran, worst, worst_case, over, refused = 0, 0.0, None, 0, []
+    for case in grid:
+        try:
+            held, ds, power = first_step(*case)
+        except Exception as exc:  # a refusal is a precondition failure, reported
+            refused.append((case, repr(exc)[:120]))
+            continue
+        ran += 1
+        outdoor = case[-1]
+        if not min(outdoor, TARGET_C) - 1e-9 <= held.room_temperature <= TARGET_C:
+            refused.append((case, f"held room {held.room_temperature:.3f} out of range"))
+        if abs(ds) > abs(worst):
+            worst, worst_case = ds, (*case, round(held.room_temperature, 3), round(power, 3))
+        over += abs(ds) > 0.02
+    print(f"RESULT census: cases {ran} of {len(grid)}, worst first-step dS {worst:+.4f} kWh_th "
+          f"at {worst_case}, over 0.02 kWh_th {over}")
+    for mode in ("none", "manual"):
+        for pump_kw in (4.0, 9.0):
+            held, ds, power = first_step(mode, True, None, pump_kw, 40.0, -25.0)
+            print(f"RESULT control two-zone -25 C mode={mode} pump {pump_kw} kW: held room "
+                  f"{held.room_temperature:.3f} power {power:.3f} first-step dS {ds:+.4f} kWh_th")
+    for case, why in refused[:10]:
+        print("REFUSED", case, why)
+    return 1 if refused or ran != len(grid) else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..7378ba0b6f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,222 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# R10-HOTFIX-TICK-SELFTEST-CHECKOUT: tick_loop.sh's self-test must read and move
+# no checkout but scratch clones of its own, whatever its caller's checkout,
+# GIT_DIR or PATH. The finder's control (the self-test run from a checkout
+# behind origin/main: a branch fails a row, a detached head is moved) and the
+# mutants that take each guard back out, on <rev>'s copy of the script.
+#
+#   bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh <rev> [arm...]
+#
+# Nothing runs in the caller's checkout: <rev>'s tick_loop.sh, heartbeat.sh,
+# ref_privacy.py and tests/throwaway_git.sh are written to a scratch directory
+# and every self-test runs from there or from a throwaway clone of it.
+#
+# Shape arms -- <rev>'s self-test run from a throwaway clone, its nested rows
+# skipped (the clone is the nesting); each prints
+#   <arm> behind=<n>: <the self-test's tally line> HEAD-MOVED|HEAD-UNMOVED
+# and the failing rows:
+#   branch    a branch clone one commit behind origin/main on tick_loop.sh
+#   detached  the same clone, detached
+#   gitdir    a detached clone behind, named by GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE (a git hook's environment)
+#   shim      a branch clone at origin/main, the state dir's bin holding a gh with the seat shim's marker (a live seat's)
+#   level     a branch clone at origin/main: the null control
+# Every arm but shim runs under a scratch HPO_STATE_DIR whose bin holds a plain gh, so the
+# caller's own gh, shim or not, decides nothing.
+# Mutant arms -- <rev>'s whole self-test from a scratch copy that is no checkout,
+# one guard taken back out; each prints `<arm>: <tally line> rc=<n>` and the failing rows:
+#   whole       no mutation: the control every mutant is read against
+#   nocheckout  the HPO_TICK_CODE_DIR export back below the TICK-GH rows
+#   gitenv      throwaway_git_env back below the heartbeat rows
+#   plaingh     the no-shim row's own plain gh taken off its PATH
+#   envscrub    the line dropping the caller's HPO_TICK_* and HPO_SWEEP_MANDATE deleted (a rev before envi)
+#   envi        the re-exec under env -i dropped: --self-test runs the rows in the caller's environment
+#   carry       the re-exec copies one caller variable through (SPY_REAL_GIT, round 3's first channel)
+#   pathfirst   the seat-bin PATH computed above the re-exec and carried by it (round 3's second channel)
+#   allowlist   the rows' entry point lets a name off the allowlist through (a rev before the re-cut)
+#   pipefail    the self-test's `set +o pipefail` deleted
+#   failopen    the refusal after the re-exec replaced by a run of the rows: a --self-test whose re-exec a
+#               caller's function named exec skipped runs every row in the caller's environment (round 4)
+#   bound       pr_args.sh's self-test bound (main's 38aee2235a) deleted from the rows' entry
+# Channel arm -- <rev>'s whole self-test from a scratch copy, once per channel a caller has into the
+# process before line 1 and at the re-exec, every run beside a scratch bare repository named as
+# HPO_HEARTBEAT_REMOTE and TICK_RC=1 (either acts if a row runs in the caller's environment); each prints
+#   channels <channel>: <the run's last line> rc=<n> fn-calls=<n> victim-refs=<n>
+#   fn-all      an exported function for every bash builtin but exec and every command the script runs,
+#               each touching a file when called (a bare redirection, so it looks up no command itself)
+#   bashenv-all the same functions defined by a BASH_ENV file
+#   fn-exec     an exported exec that skips the /usr/bin/env call (the round-4 attack)
+#   posix       fn-exec under POSIXLY_CORRECT, and under SHELLOPTS=posix: exec is a special builtin there
+#   noexec      SHELLOPTS=noexec: bash runs no line of any script
+#   opts        SHELLOPTS=errexit:nounset:xtrace and BASHOPTS=execfail:extglob
+#   env         ENV naming a file that touches one when sourced
+#   path        PATH led by a directory whose bash, env, git and python3 touch a file
+#   ifs         IFS=/ in the caller
+# A mutant arm needs the `# mut:selftest-*` markers and says so on a <rev> without them.
+# No arm named runs the five shapes.
+set -uo pipefail
+rev=${1:?usage: r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh <rev> [branch|detached|gitdir|shim|level|whole|nocheckout|gitenv|plaingh|envscrub|envi|carry|pathfirst|allowlist|pipefail|failopen|bound|channels]...}; shift
+[ $# -gt 0 ] || set -- branch detached gitdir shim level
+top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || exit 2
+sha=$(git -C "$top" rev-parse --verify -q "$rev^{commit}") || { echo "no commit $rev"; exit 2; }
+d=$(mktemp -d) || exit 2
+trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
+L=tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh
+extract() { # <dir>: <rev>'s six files, in a directory that is no checkout
+  local f; mkdir -p "$1/tools/audit/seat" "$1/tests"
+  for f in "$L" tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py tools/audit/seat/offline_spy.py tests/throwaway_git.sh tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh; do
+    git -C "$top" show "$sha:$f" > "$1/$f" 2>/dev/null || [ "$f" = tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh ] || exit 2
+  done
+}
+extract "$d/src"
+# shellcheck source=/dev/null
+. "$d/src/tests/throwaway_git.sh"
+mkdir -p "$d/plain/bin" "$d/shim/bin"
+printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$d/plain/bin/gh"; printf '#!/bin/sh\n# hpo-gh-shim\nexit 0\n' > "$d/shim/bin/gh"
+chmod +x "$d/plain/bin/gh" "$d/shim/bin/gh"
+bare() { env -u HPO_TICK_CODE_DIR -u HPO_TICK_HEARTBEAT -u GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES HPO_STATE_DIR="$d/plain" "$@"; }
+rows() { sed -n 's/^  FAIL /    FAIL /p; s/^    nested FAIL: /      nested FAIL: /p' "$1"; }
+
+clones() { # the scratch origin, one commit ahead of the `old` clone on tick_loop.sh
+  [ -d "$d/o.git" ] && return 0
+  (
+    throwaway_git_env
+    cp -R "$d/src" "$d/n"
+    throwaway_git_init "$d/o.git" -q --bare -b main && throwaway_git_init "$d/n" -q -b main || exit 2
+    git -C "$d/n" add -A && git -C "$d/n" commit -qm base && git -C "$d/o.git" fetch -q "$d/n" main:main || exit 2
+    throwaway_git_clone -q "$d/o.git" "$d/old" || exit 2
+    printf '# ahead\n' >> "$d/n/$L"
+    git -C "$d/n" commit -qam ahead && git -C "$d/o.git" fetch -q "$d/n" main:main || exit 2
+    throwaway_git_clone -q "$d/o.git" "$d/new" || exit 2
+  ) || { echo "the scratch clones could not be built"; exit 2; }
+}
+
+shape() { # <arm>
+  local arm=$1 c=$d/c-$1 h0 h1 n m
+  local -a pre=()
+  clones; rm -rf "$c"
+  case $arm in
+    branch) cp -R "$d/old" "$c" ;;
+    detached) cp -R "$d/old" "$c"; (throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" checkout -q --detach) ;;
+    gitdir) cp -R "$d/old" "$c"; (throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" checkout -q --detach); pre=(GIT_DIR="$c/.git" GIT_WORK_TREE="$c") ;;
+    shim) cp -R "$d/new" "$c"; pre=(HPO_STATE_DIR="$d/shim") ;;
+    level) cp -R "$d/new" "$c" ;;
+  esac
+  h0=$(throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" rev-parse HEAD)
+  HPO_TICK_SELFTEST_NESTED=1 bare ${pre[@]+"${pre[@]}"} bash "$c/$L" --self-test --nested > "$d/$arm.log" 2>&1
+  h1=$(throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" rev-parse HEAD)
+  n=$(throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" fetch -q origin main; git -C "$c" rev-list --count "$h0..origin/main")
+  [ "$h0" = "$h1" ] && m=HEAD-UNMOVED || m=HEAD-MOVED
+  echo "$arm behind=$n: $(tail -n 1 "$d/$arm.log") $m"; rows "$d/$arm.log"
+}
+
+mutant() { # <arm>
+  local arm=$1 m=$d/m-$1 rc
+  rm -rf "$m"; extract "$m"
+  python3 - "$m/$L" "$arm" 2>/dev/null <<'PY' || { echo "$arm: NOT RUN, the mutation did not apply (no '# mut:selftest-*' marker at this rev?)"; return; }
+import sys
+p, arm = sys.argv[1:]
+s = open(p).read().split("\n")
+def marked(marker):
+    g = [i for i, l in enumerate(s) if l.rstrip().endswith("# mut:" + marker)]
+    assert len(g) == 1, (marker, g)
+    return g[0]
+def move(marker, after):  # the marked line, back to where the merge base ran it
+    line = s.pop(marked(marker))
+    a = [i for i, l in enumerate(s) if after in l]
+    assert len(a) == 1, (after, a)
+    s.insert(a[0] + 1, line)
+if arm == "nocheckout":
+    move("selftest-nocheckout", 'ck "a seat bin dir with no gh shim')
+elif arm == "gitenv":
+    move("selftest-gitenv", "# The real script against a bare remote")
+elif arm == "plaingh":
+    i = marked("selftest-plaingh")
+    assert 'PATH="$t/bare:$PATH" ' in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace('PATH="$t/bare:$PATH" ', "")
+elif arm == "envscrub":
+    s.pop(marked("selftest-envscrub"))
+elif arm == "envi":
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    s[i] = '  tick_loop_self_test  # mut:selftest-envi' if "selftest_allowlisted" in "\n".join(s) else ""
+elif arm == "carry":
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    assert "env -i PATH=" in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace("env -i PATH=", 'env -i SPY_REAL_GIT="${SPY_REAL_GIT-}" PATH=')
+elif arm == "pathfirst":
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    lit = 'PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:${BASH%/*}"'
+    assert lit in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace(lit, 'PATH="$PATH"')
+    k = marked("seatbin")
+    assert s[k - 1].startswith("SEAT_BIN=") and s[k + 1] == "export PATH"
+    block = s[k - 1:k + 2]
+    del s[k - 1:k + 2]
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    s[i:i] = block
+elif arm == "allowlist":
+    i = marked("selftest-allowlist")
+    assert '*" $v "*) ;; *)' in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace('*" $v "*) ;; *)', '*) ;; *" $v "*)')
+elif arm == "pipefail":
+    s.pop(marked("selftest-pipefail"))
+elif arm == "failopen":
+    i = marked("selftest-failclosed")
+    assert s[i].startswith("case ${1:-} in --self-test) refused=")
+    s[i] = 'case ${1:-} in --self-test) set -- --self-test-rows "${@:2}" ;; esac  # mut:selftest-failclosed'
+elif arm == "bound":
+    i = marked("selftest-bound")
+    assert "pr_bounded tick_loop" in s[i]
+    del s[i]
+else:
+    assert arm == "whole"
+open(p, "w").write("\n".join(s))
+PY
+  bash -n "$m/$L" || { echo "$arm: NOT RUN, the mutant does not parse"; return; }
+  bare bash "$m/$L" --self-test > "$d/$arm.log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+  echo "$arm: $(tail -n 1 "$d/$arm.log") rc=$rc"; rows "$d/$arm.log"
+}
+
+channels() { # every channel in parallel, one line each
+  local c b=$BASH x=$d/ch o
+  mkdir -p "$x"
+  local -a names=() fenv=()
+  while read -r o; do [ "$o" = exec ] || names+=("$o"); done < <(compgen -b)
+  names+=(git mktemp python3 sed grep env bash head tr cat chmod mkdir cp rm mv date sleep timeout kill tail wc cut sort dirname pwd)
+  run1() { # <channel> [env args...]: one whole self-test under that caller
+    local c=$1 v=$x/victim-$1.git rc; shift
+    mkdir -p "$x/calls-$c"; (throwaway_git_env; throwaway_git_init "$v" -q --bare) || return
+    (cd "$x" && env HPO_HEARTBEAT_REMOTE="$v" TICK_RC=1 "$@" "$d/src/$L" --self-test) > "$x/$c.log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+    echo "channels $c: $(tail -n 1 "$x/$c.log") rc=$rc fn-calls=$(ls "$x/calls-$c" | grep -c .) victim-refs=$(git -C "$v" for-each-ref | grep -c .)" > "$x/$c.line"; }
+  fdefs() { # <channel>: the function corpus, as a BASH_ENV file's text
+    local i=0 n; for n in "${names[@]}"; do i=$((i + 1)); printf '%s() { >> %q; }\n' "$n" "$x/calls-$1/fn-$i-${n//[^a-z0-9]/_}"; done; }
+  while IFS= read -r c; do fenv+=("BASH_FUNC_${c%%()*}%%=()${c#*()}"); done < <(fdefs fn-all)
+  printf 'exec() { if [ "${1:-}" = /usr/bin/env ]; then >> %q; return 0; fi; builtin exec "$@"; }\n' "$x/calls-shellopts-posix/exec" > "$x/execfn-posix"
+  fdefs bashenv-all > "$x/bashenv-all"; echo ">> $x/calls-env/sourced" > "$x/envfile"
+  mkdir -p "$x/pbin"; for o in bash env git python3; do printf '#!/bin/sh\n>> %q\nexit 1\n' "$x/calls-path/$o" > "$x/pbin/$o"; chmod +x "$x/pbin/$o"; done
+  run1 fn-all "${fenv[@]}" "$b" & run1 bashenv-all BASH_ENV="$x/bashenv-all" "$b" &
+  run1 fn-exec "BASH_FUNC_exec%%=() { if [ \"\${1:-}\" = /usr/bin/env ]; then >> $x/calls-fn-exec/exec; return 0; fi; builtin exec \"\$@\"; }" "$b" &
+  run1 posix POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 "BASH_FUNC_exec%%=() { if [ \"\${1:-}\" = /usr/bin/env ]; then >> $x/calls-posix/exec; return 0; fi; builtin exec \"\$@\"; }" "$b" &
+  run1 shellopts-posix SHELLOPTS=posix BASH_ENV="$x/execfn-posix" "$b" &
+  run1 noexec SHELLOPTS=noexec "$b" & run1 opts SHELLOPTS=errexit:nounset:xtrace BASHOPTS=execfail:extglob "$b" &
+  run1 env ENV="$x/envfile" "$b" & run1 path PATH="$x/pbin:$PATH" "$b" & run1 ifs IFS=/ "$b" &
+  wait; cat "$x"/*.line
+  # The null controls: each channel's instrument records a call when one is made.
+  local -a fctl=(); mkdir -p "$x/calls-fn-ctl" "$x/calls-bashenv-ctl" "$x/calls-env-ctl" "$x/calls-path-ctl" "$x/qbin"
+  while IFS= read -r c; do fctl+=("BASH_FUNC_${c%%()*}%%=()${c#*()}"); done < <(fdefs fn-ctl)
+  env "${fctl[@]}" "$b" -c 'cd /; git status; mktemp; exit 0'
+  fdefs bashenv-ctl > "$x/bashenv-ctl"; env BASH_ENV="$x/bashenv-ctl" "$b" -c 'cd /; git status; mktemp; exit 0'
+  echo ">> $x/calls-env-ctl/sourced" > "$x/envfile-ctl"; env ENV="$x/envfile-ctl" "$b" --posix -i -c : 2>/dev/null
+  printf '#!/bin/sh\n>> %q\n' "$x/calls-path-ctl/git" > "$x/qbin/git"; chmod +x "$x/qbin/git"; env PATH="$x/qbin:$PATH" "$b" -c 'git status'
+  for c in fn bashenv env path; do echo "channels null control $c: fn-calls=$(ls "$x/calls-$c-ctl" | grep -c .)"; done
+  echo "channels corpus: ${#names[@]} function names"
+}
+
+echo "rev $sha"
+for arm in "$@"; do
+  case $arm in
+    branch|detached|gitdir|shim|level) shape "$arm" ;;
+    whole|nocheckout|gitenv|plaingh|envscrub|envi|carry|pathfirst|allowlist|pipefail|failopen|bound) mutant "$arm" ;;
+    channels) channels ;;
+    *) echo "unknown arm '$arm'"; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done

Do not start a second fixer when that group's fixer worktree was written in the last 15 minutes. A pull request the overlay holds is not returned by this step.

A conclusion of failure returns that pull request to its original fixer this turn, with the job URL and failure line, unless `merge_train.py classify <head> --pr <N>` reads it WAIT (a gate deferral). `ci-watch.sh` alerts only on a new signature, so a red it printed is still owed: the signature file is not this check. Pending, `nightly-status` and `delivery-status` are not a return. Zero check runs is stalled zero-runs: `tools/pr/approve_held_runs.sh`, not a fixer. Read the autofix summary before returning a closures or mutation failure, under the same words as step 11. -    "Moved from R10-COP-GATE-E carry 1 (0-based) by the carries-open audit (orchestrator s13, 2026-11-09): not measurable from the recorded fixtures (PR 3371); a round-11 D15 input that waits on named owner data. Original text: Unanswered residual of R10-CEILING-PROBE Carry 1, from #2465 (handoff-body/r10-ceiling-probe 61b216fc; orchestrator s9 2026-10-31). The gain between set-point and drawn power at levels between the duty gate and the ceiling is unmeasured: the probe measures only the draw at the ceiling, as its approved note scopes it. #2465 routed this gap to R10-DEMAND-OVERBOOK, which is done, and carry_audit refuses a done destination. It is re-routed here because R10-COP-GATE is the live group that owns the DrawRange and power modelling and runs after the probe. Measure first: from the probe's stored samples plus ordinary operation, report whether drawn power tracks the set-point linearly between gate and ceiling, with a flat-price null control. Only if it does not, build the correction, or record a refusal with the number. The measurement needs no new owner data if the recorded fixtures carry enough operating points: drive it with a harness on the recorded fixtures (`dev/audit/harnesses/draw_range_evidence.py` and `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_cop_gate_top.py` are the starting instruments) and report the fitted gain between set-point and drawn power over the band between the duty gate and the ceiling, with the flat-price null. If the fixtures cannot span that band, the body states exactly which readings are missing (set-point, drawn power, band, count of steps) and the owner data that closes it (a diagnostics download with the week of debug data on, from an install whose pump ran across the band), and the carry stays open on that named data, not on a deferral. -    "From r10-outside-learner-robustness-p2, body item 4b518e5d: Round 11: the scaled settling tail. Measured on `dev/audit/harnesses/boost_press_tail_walk.py` (table above, both slopes, with the heat-free `freeze` twins as the null control): neither formula keeps every press arm within `press_120x1_full`'s |worst| on `tests/boost_drift_replay.py`'s replay. The freeze with no heat walks the scale as far as the press does (-0.0232 vs -0.0237), so the walk is the freeze's sample selection, not the heat. The walk is also not monotone in the tail (press 10x1: +0.0028 at a 1.5 h tail, -0.0237 at 4.55 h). Precondition a future formula must meet: every press arm of the harness within the absolute bound under `slope<new>` at its own merge base, re-measured and not carried from these figures, plus an explanation of the freeze-skip walk (why a heat-free freeze of these hours moves the interval learner, and why the formula's arms are not tuned to this scenario's hours). After the rebase, the head carries dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md, but review_packet refuses the dispatch with \"head-note: ## Head does not name the dispatched head\", because dependabot rewrites the body on every rebase. body_patch.sh, the instrument that repairs a body without moving the head, then refuses on \"no commit list was read for this Dependabot pull request (--commits-file)\". It never passes one, so a dependabot body cannot be patched at all. This was hit on #3088 at bffd45a03. Two fixes, either sufficient: body_patch.sh reads the PR's commit list and passes --commits-file for a dependabot PR; or review_packet's head-note check accepts a dependabot PR whose commits are all dependabot's and whose head carries its delivery row.      "From triage batch 155 (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch155.md#P566 at 1a3e60ac78), queue line S14-RELAY-CADENCE, option (c), a repair of an observed wrong behaviour. Build it with this group's P546 carry (handoff-wip dispose), which changes the same arm. tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh carry_fold_arm writes cloud-folded only on success (line 843) and checks it by \"<topic> <bsha>\" (line 821), where bsha is the tip of handoff-wip/<topic>-body. On each failure, body_push.sh keeps the refused body as a new parentless commit (body_push.sh line 106). So r10-train-residue's fold re-ran body_push (at least 60 s each) on every relay pass and pushed a new kept commit each time: d982cc00b7, 2cfd2407be, ef11984257 and 7d1f0419ad between 01:20Z and 02:17Z, all with tree 6ae9f4ff2db8 and BODY.md blob 80dc1f17dc70. Meanwhile its body had already reached PR 3424 (handoff-body/r10-train-residue 2fa8399213, BODIED 01:44:40Z). A memo keyed on the kept commit would never hit. Fix: a failed fold or body_push records \"<topic> <stop sha> <BODY.md blob sha> <handoff/<topic> tip> <refusal last line>\" in <state>/cloud-fold-failed. A pass skips a stop whose stop sha, BODY.md blob and handoff/<topic> tip all equal a record, and prints \"cloud_relay: OWED carry-fold <topic> unchanged since <utc>: <line>\" so the level still owes it. A change to any of the three re-runs it as today. Self-test: the train-residue shape (a new kept commit with the same blob, the same stop and code tip) is skipped; a changed blob, or a moved handoff tip, re-runs; null control: a stop with no record runs as today; a mutant keyed on the kept commit sha fails the first case.",
     "From triage batch 156 (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch156.md#P568 at 23c4d90aa2), queue line S14-PACKET-REFUSES-DEFERRAL-RED, a repair of an observed wrong behaviour (a class: 14 dispatch outputs hold the refusal on gate; today PRs 3424, 3404, 3429). tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py main gathers read = required_reading(a.pr, head) whenever a required context is red (line 602 at 63bcdcaad8), which is merge_train.py classify --pr, the answer bus.sh dispatch uses. build turns a WAIT or GREEN read into a required-wait or required-green advisory for the required-red arm (lines 544-557, #3379). But the red-unanswered arm (lines 542-543) refuses the same gate red from unanswered_reds(..., gate[2], ...) without consulting the read. Reproduced at about 02:50Z: classify 561edf4c8f --pr 3404 and classify 498c2ab042 --pr 3429 both read \"WAIT ... pending: gate red: none\" beside completed-failure gate check-runs of edit runs (42945740958; 42946500173 and 42946386595), and bus3404.out and bus3429.out both refused \"red-unanswered: concluded red check `gate` is not named in ## Red checks\". Fix: in build, an entry of facts[\"red_unanswered\"] that is in REQUIRED gets no red-unanswered refusal when facts[\"required_read\"]'s word is WAIT or GREEN; its required-wait or required-green advisory already names it. A RED, APPROVAL-OWED or unreadable read, and any red outside REQUIRED, keep today's refusal. Do not add a second classify call (Train.classify_at or otherwise): the read at line 602 decides, and a second read costs API calls and could disagree with the first. A local version under s14/tools-wt-63bcdcaa calls classify_at again; build the permanent form on the existing read. Self-test: red_unanswered=[\"gate\"] with required_read (\"WAIT\", \"pending: gate red: none\") renders one required-wait advisory and no refusal; the same with (\"RED\", ...) refuses red-unanswered and required-red; null control: a non-required red (\"tests / fast\") with a WAIT read still refuses red-unanswered; a mutant dropping the WAIT/GREEN condition fails the first case.      "From triage batch 162 (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch162.md#P575 at 98099a02a3), queue line DISPOSE-NEVER-CLEARS-BOARD, arm (a2), a repair of an observed wrong behaviour; build it with this group's P546 carry (handoff-wip dispose and orphans honouring dispositions), which changes the same orphan arm. This carry adds tools/audit/seat/ledger.py to the group's files (no open group owns it). Cause: ledger.py covered() (line 393 at main dbd1ab5b07) returns False when the merge-base..tip diff is empty (\"if rc or not names.strip(): return False\"), and reverse_applies has no patch, so landed() (line 464) returns None for a tip whose net change is nothing; bus.sh orphans and the relay's level both classify through landed(). Instance: handoff/r10-body-contract-p3-bootstrap cdad1183b2, 0 files in its three-dot diff against main, 3 '+' commits in git cherry (an add-then-remove pair), STRANDED for 30 h and disposed 5 times. Fix: an empty merge-base..tip diff read with rc 0 lands, as its own named reason (for example \"empty\") ahead of \"content\"; rc != 0 stays not-landed. Self-test arms: the add-then-remove net-empty shape lands as empty; mutant dropping the branch makes it STRANDED again; null control: a tip with one real uncovered line stays None. Do not add a \"handoff or PR head newer than BLOCKED\" rule for blocked stops (REJECTED in the ruling: 0 of the 3 named stops would clear).",
     "From triage batch 162 (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch162.md#P576 at 98099a02a3), queue line PENDING-CI-RED-DEADLOCK, a repair of an observed wrong behaviour (PR 3419, relay overridden once with HPO_RELAY_CLASSIFY; PR 3425 at c6becb31 next). Cause: tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh's pending-ci block (lines 259-275 at main dbd1ab5b07) dies on a moved head (line 268) before any carry test, while line 405 already relays a verdict across a range review_carry.py answers CARRY; a red the branch did not cause and only a main merge cures is refused at line 273 before the cure and at line 268 after it. Fix: at line 268, before refusing a moved head, run ${HPO_RELAY_CARRY:-python3 -I review_carry.py} <drafted head> <live head> --verdict-only; on CARRY classify the LIVE head and post on GREEN, saying in the relay line that the verdict was carried; on FRESH-REVIEW or CANNOT DECIDE keep today's refusal and re-dispatch; RED at the live head still refuses. Self-test (pending-ci arms near lines 1183-1190, reusing the carry-ok/no/un stubs at 1161-1163): moved head + carry-ok + GREEN posts; moved head + carry-no refuses; null control same head + GREEN posts as today; mutant skipping the carry call makes the carry-ok arm refuse.",
-    "From triage batch 166 (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch166.md#P580 at ef2659ab89), queue line CARRY-FOLD-ARM-REJUDGES-EVERY-PASS, a cost repair measured at about 30% of the relay pass. Cause: tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh carry_fold_arm (lines 805-850 at main a7628041dc) fetches and shows BLOCKED.md for every handoff-wip/<topic> ref on every pass (line 818; 27-33 s for 46 topics on 2026-11-11), and records only a successful fold in cloud-folded (line 843), so a fold whose body_push.sh fails after carry_fold.py succeeded re-runs carry_fold.py and body_push.sh every pass (2 topics, about 181 s a pass). Fix: a judged-outcome memo, state file cloud-fold-judged, one line per topic: <topic> <wip sha> <body sha> <outcome> <epoch>. (1) Take both shas from the ls-remote the arm already makes; a topic whose (wip sha, body sha) is in the memo is neither fetched nor shown. (2) Re-write its stored OWED level line into cloud-level-fold.$$, because level_set (line 849) replaces the whole carry-fold level each pass and a dropped line clears an owed item silently. (3) A failure after the fold (carry_fold rc != 0 or body_push rc != 0) is retried only once its memo entry is 3600 s old, because an ancestry red can clear with no ref moving. (4) Success still appends to cloud-folded.
